title: Sam Parr: Selling The Hustle to HubSpot and growing a newsletter to 2M subscribers
summary: Sam Parr explains how The Hustle grew to nearly 2M subscribers, what due diligence on the HubSpot sale was like, and how he hires and hands off. He gives concrete advice on paid newsletters: charge more, bill annually, and use a long-form sales page as your homepage.

principles.text: Charge far more for paid newsletters; higher prices raise revenue and make customers value the product more.
principles.quote: If you actually want to make a living at this and provide value, you got to charge more money. How are you going to make a living if you're charging $4 a month?

principles.text: Push annual billing only; if you offer monthly, price it high as an anchor so annual is a no-brainer.
principles.quote: if you're going to awfully offer a monthly price, make it like crazy expensive so it puts an anchor so it makes the annual a no-brainer.

principles.text: Make a long-form sales page your homepage and gate checkout behind an email capture to build a lead list.
principles.quote: I would make it so you have to enter your email to see the next the checkout page because what's the average conversion rate? Like 3%, but you can collect probably 10 or 12% of those people's email

principles.text: Finding acquisition sources matters as much as content; co-registration partnerships can be paid per lead or only for engaged users.
principles.quote: people think if you have good content, you're going to make it. It's acquiring users is it's like is as important as the content.

principles.text: Start new things yourself, then hand them to skilled operators, set targets, and only step in when asked for help.
principles.quote: I'm the type of guy who I like to start stuff and then hand it off.

principles.text: Study profitable direct-response operators like Agora and Motley Fool and apply their tactics ethically, rather than copying Substack peers.
principles.quote: let's figure out what they're doing that's really good and make apply that to a good product with a high integrity team.
